subject: TEST-NUMVAL-F function
notes:
PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB256, 2026-09-13). Both grounds of the downgrade are discharged, and the folded 1) b) 5. — which had NO test of any kind, in any mode, because nothing in tests/ wrote an exponent of more than one digit — now has three.
(1) ⛔ THE NORMATIVE TENSION IS RESOLVED AND RECORDED, which is what the PARTIAL was really for: the implementation chose between two readings in silence and the choice changes the answer. §15.69.3 r5 ('Embedded spaces in argument-1 are ignored except between the first numeric digit and the last digit that precedes a letter E' — cite.py --check 15.69.3 -> OK, rule 5) excepts only the SIGNIFICAND, and read as ELIDE-AND-JOIN it would make TEST-NUMVAL-F("1E+1 2345") a five-digit exponent answering 9. WiseOwl COBOL answers 6, and that is now a stated determination in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 with a comment at the exponent loop, on two independent grounds. (a) §15.69.3 r1's figure — RENDERED from the printed page 898, since a general-format diagram was load-bearing — draws n as ONE contiguous metavariable ('n is one, two, three, or four digits representing the exponent' — --check OK, rule 1) with [ space-string ] only BEFORE and AFTER it, so the space is the legal trailing space-string and the '2' after it is simply outside the format. (b) §15.95.4 r1 b) 1 governs the case DIRECTLY and is unqualified as to which run — 'if one or more spaces are embedded within a string of numeric characters, the returned value is the position of the first non-space character following the spaces' (--check OK, 1) b) 1.) — where sub-notes 2, 3 and 4 of that same list each say 'of the significand' explicitly. The drafters distinguished inside one list. WITNESSED by conformance:cases/15.95.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_f_spaces, which is discriminating in both directions: EIN4 "1E+1 234" = 6 (the joined reading answers 0 — it would be a CONFORMING four-digit exponent), EIN5 "1E+1 2345" = 6 (the joined reading answers 9), and the figure's legal slots are pinned beside them — EBEF "1E+ 1234" = 0, EAFT "1E+1234 " = 0, ALLSP " + 1.5E + 1 " = 0 — so the determination cannot be satisfied by a scanner that simply rejects every space.
(2) THE STANDARD-BINARY HALF is the PB198 decline, recorded per-row and NOT by widening the standard-binary-only selector (this rule is not conditioned solely on the mode). Annex A.3 item 2 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY processor-dependent, §4.2.6 gives the discretion not to claim support plus the duty to warn and document, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §1/§2 documents it. ⛔ The refuter's objection — that the decline was argued about the CODE rather than proved on this rule's own path — is answered by a new fixture rather than by the same argument: conformance:cases/15.95.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256-standard-binary-test-numval-f names TEST-NUMVAL-F itself under OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY. and is reject-at 2014 2023 (COBOL0806), the twin of the TEST-NUMVAL fixture whose header states exactly that discipline.
(3) THE FOLDED 1) b) 5. IS MEASURED FOR THE FIRST TIME, in both of the modes at issue: conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_standard_decimal NFEXP "1E+12345" = 8 under the mode the sub-note names, and pb256_test_numval_f_spaces EFIVE the same under native (where §15.69.3 r1's where-clause caps n at four digits with no mode qualification, so leg b) generic lands on the same character). Sub-note 4's own verdict is measured beside it — NF32 = 0, NF34 = 0, NF35 = 35 — as a boundary pair, which is the only shape that can tell 34 from 31 or 35; NF32 is the discriminator, since native answers 32 for that argument.
(4) THE FOLDED 1) b) 6. capacity leg keeps its landed PB121 evidence, and 1) b) 1's significand half is pinned by SIG1 "0 1E+2" = 3, §15.95.4's OWN verbatim example, which no fixture had carried at golden level. Leg c) and its NOTE are measured by conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_leg_c_and_national (FZ = 1, FSP = 5, FIN = 4, plus FE "1E" = 3 and FES "1E+" = 4 — a dangling E is incomplete, not a character in error).
(5) THE COMPILER-SIDE commaMode ARM, unmeasured for this function too, is now end to end: conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/pb256_test_numval_mode_flags P3/P4 (no clause) against D3/D4 (DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA) is the mirror pair — "1,5E+1" moves from 2 to 0 and "1.5E+1" from 0 to 2. IntrinsicModeFlagCoverageDriftTests keeps every such arm covered as new ones appear.
EDITION GATE: conformance:cases/15.93.4-Returned-value-rule/test_validators_below_2002 now names TEST-NUMVAL-F (COBOL1502 at 85); it was the one member of the validator quartet that fixture did not name.
